description: A book editor for Minecraft that writes ordinary vanilla books.

mods.name: Roleplayer's Quill
mods.description: A book editor for people who write in Minecraft. Select a passage and set it bold, coloured, underlined, or aligned left, centre, right or justified – laid out to the pixel with the game's own spaces, so the finished book reads the same for everyone, with no mod and no resource pack. Paste a chapter in and it flows across as many pages as it needs, hyphenated by the rules of Russian or English if you want the lines full. Lists, tables, a character browser, a format brush, import and export to a file, and voice typing that runs offline on your own machine. Replaces the sign, anvil and chat editors too. Client side only.

releases.notes:
## Typing over a selection no longer crashes the game

Selecting text across several paragraphs and typing over it lost the first letter, and the second one crashed the game. The letter went into a paragraph the selection had already folded away, leaving the caret past the end of the line. Typing over a selection now replaces it as it should.

releases.notes:
## Symbols and Shift on the arrows

Two new symbol shelves. Faces and hearts: ☺ ☹ ☻ ツ ❤, pointing and writing hands, the bits kaomoji are built from, and the game's own 🗡 🏹 🪓 🔱 🎣 🧪. Circled: ➀ to ➉, ① to ⑳, Ⓐ to ⓩ. Everything else Stendhal offered and this mod did not is now on the shelf it belongs on, and the search reaches the emoji the game's font draws.

Shift on a page arrow goes to the first or the last page. It works in this editor, in a signed book, on a lectern and in the game's own editor, and Shift with Page Up or Page Down does the same. On the last page Shift with the forward arrow does nothing rather than add a page.

releases.notes:
## Bookmarks

Every book can now hold one bookmark. It hangs from the top of the page, left of the page number: click the empty spot there to mark the page, click the ribbon to take it out. On any other page only its end shows over the edge of the book, and clicking it turns straight to the marked page. The page list shows the bookmark too, and can set it.

A book opens at its bookmark, written or signed. The new setting "Open at the bookmark" turns that off, and the book opens on its first page as before. A lectern never opens at it by itself, because a lectern's page turns for everyone standing at it.

Right click the bookmark to change its colour and shape for that book alone: a silk ribbon, a cord with a tassel, a leather strap, twin ribbons or a quill feather, in ten colours. The settings choose what a new bookmark looks like.

Bookmarks are kept on your computer, in `config/roleplayersquill/bookmarks.json`, and never written into the book, so nobody else's copy changes.

releases.notes:
## The up arrow in chat brings back your last message again

With the symbol row over the chat box, pressing the up arrow to bring back the last message also moved the keyboard focus onto the first button of the row, and its tooltip covered the chat. The buttons of every toolbar are for the mouse, so they no longer take the focus from the keyboard at all, and the arrows stay with whatever is being typed.

releases.notes:
## Copy, paste and clear on signs

Three buttons to the left of the sign in the sign editor, as Stendhal has them. Copy puts the sign on the clipboard, one row to a line. Paste writes the clipboard back onto the sign, all four rows at once: a row the clipboard has no line for is emptied, and a line too wide for the sign is cut where the sign would stop taking letters. Clear empties all four rows. The buttons live under the same setting as the symbol row on signs.

One jar, Minecraft 1.21.6 to 1.21.8, Fabric, client side only.

Formats a book the way a word processor does and writes an ordinary vanilla book: anyone can read it without the mod and without a resource pack.

Requires Fabric API. Cloth Config and Mod Menu are optional. Java 21.

Speech recognition is offline and optional; the engine and the model are downloaded on first use and are not inside this jar.
